tools.name: get_compute_status
tools.description: Check whether the GPU provider can accept audio transcription work. Returns availability, permitted task types, and limits. Does not start a job.

tools.name: submit_compute_job
tools.description: Beta users must supply their uploaded asset_id and kind compute_job. No accuracy guarantee is made for uploaded files. tools.name: get_compute_job
tools.description: Read a previously submitted job by job_id. Returns status, transcript, runtime and reference quality when complete. For queued or running jobs, wait poll_after_seconds before checking again. Failed or expired jobs are not successful results.

tools.name: get_service_status
tools.description: Public live availability, model catalog, free-trial limits and polling guidance. No token required. Check before submitting; an offline GPU cannot execute work.

tools.name: submit_chat_job
tools.description: Queue a free text task: draft, summarize, extract, translate text, reason or assist with code. No code is executed. tools.name: submit_image_job
tools.description: Queue a free text-to-image task from a complete scene description. Each task is independent, not an edit of a previous image. Returns a job ID; poll get_studio_job then get_studio_image for the PNG. Configured model and size appear in service status/results. No external AI fallback.

tools.name: get_studio_job
tools.description: Read your own chat/image job. Includes partial text while running, final text or image availability, GPU runtime and server timings. Wait poll_after_seconds between checks; stop on succeeded, failed or expired. Does not create or retry work.

tools.name: get_studio_image
tools.description: Return the completed image as an MCP image content block. Requires the same token/identity that submitted the job. Images expire after 24 hours from submission; download before expiry.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_trial_access" stacks urgency/override words (never, bypass). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_compute_job, get_studio_job · Private data: create_trial_access, submit_compute_job, get_service_status, get_studio_image · Public sink: create_trial_access, submit_compute_job, submit_chat_job, submit_image_job · Destructive: get_service_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_compute_job, get_studio_job · Private data: create_trial_access, submit_compute_job, get_service_status, get_studio_image · Public sink: create_trial_access, submit_compute_job, submit_chat_job, submit_image_job · Destructive: get_service_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
